title: Bake the high-poly scan normals onto the body plan viewer's final quad mesh
user-messages:
> 4. Which scans to test on. On master only IMG_4111 (84 labels) and IMG_4112 (54) carry labels. IMG_4109/4110 have rings but no labels, and IMG_4113–4118 are being labelled in the six segmentation worktrees (CRAW-95…100, 24–43 labels each). I’d copy three or four of those labelled files into tmp/ to test with, rather than wait for them to land.

baking should be in separate ticket since it will be complicated
description:
User request 2026-11-07, split out of CRAW-103 (body plan viewer): after the body plan viewer joins the chosen crawfish parts with mesh booleans and the quad layout pipeline turns the result into the final quad mesh, bake the high-poly scan's surface detail (normals) onto that quad mesh so the low-poly result keeps the scans' detail. The user expects this to be complicated, which is why it is its own ticket.

Wanted: a DSL node that takes the high-poly source (the boolean-joined scan parts) and the quad mesh with its UVs, casts from the quad surface to the source, and writes a tangent-space normal map (and keeps the existing texture transfer path for colour), exportable with export_mesh to GLB.
definition-of-done:
1. A DSL node bakes a tangent-space normal map from a high-poly source onto a quad mesh with UVs, with the cage/ray distance a parameter.
2. Run on the body plan viewer's assembled crawfish quad mesh; the baked result rendered next to the high-poly source shows the scan detail; screenshots under tmp/ and a launch entry.
3. export_mesh writes the quad mesh with the normal map into a GLB that Blender opens with the map applied.
testing-plan: 1. Bake on the CRAW-103 assembled crawfish; compare renders against the high-poly source. 2. Export to GLB and open in Blender.
unknowns: Ray casting from a quad surface against a ~1M-triangle source: which existing spatial index to use.
Whether a normal map needs tangents the export path does not yet write.
